quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops gradually and smoothly.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: You can help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Maintaining a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintaining a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance by maintaining a steady speed. Also signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is necessary to react to things you see or hear on the road. Even if you are below the legal limit, any alcohol affects your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough room on the other side for you to completely cross.
The crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are transporting two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough room on the other side for you to completely cross.
questions.explanation: A train can be on any track at any time in either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop. Do not stop on the tracks.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if possible.
Drive faster to protect your right-of-way.
Always stay in your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if possible.
questions.explanation: When traffic permits, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals you to return.
You signal for three seconds.
You see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must remain stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus moves again.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus moves again.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is flashing red lights and has its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm retracts, and the bus starts moving.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you are not too close. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to the lane.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, you should consider all of these except:

options.text: Applying your brakes.
Letting go of the steering wheel.
Pressing your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Letting go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press yourself against your seat and put your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle. Do not let go of the steering wheel.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 55 mph
45 mph
65 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph
questions.explanation: On primary and secondary state and federal highways in Tennessee, the speed limit is 55 mph unless a different speed limit is posted.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what must you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings when they follow traffic signals. You must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to all vehicles coming toward you from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter. Be ready to stop, but you can continue if no traffic is coming.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit and the light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when parking next to a curb and when leaving the curb.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Only use your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Also watch traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot dangers early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot dangers early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes. Look for signals from other drivers. Watch for cars merging at on-ramps and be ready for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show traffic laws you must follow. This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: Children under ____ years old must use an approved child restraint device in a moving vehicle.

options.text: three
two
four

questions.correctAnswerText: four
questions.explanation: Children under one year old or under 20 pounds must face the rear. Children 1 to 3 years old and over 20 pounds must face forward. Children 4 to 8 years old and under 4'9" tall must use a booster seat and wear a seat belt.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: After a full stop, go through the intersection in the order you arrived. If you arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first.

questions.question: You cannot make a U-turn near a curve or hill if you cannot:

options.text: Complete the turn in 30 seconds.
See 500 feet ahead in both directions.
Drive on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: See 500 feet ahead in both directions.
questions.explanation: You cannot make a U-turn where you cannot clearly see 500 feet in both directions.

questions.question: Which factor affects how your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Body weight, sex, food in your stomach, and how much you drink all affect alcohol absorption. Only time removes alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge smoothly.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge smoothly.
questions.explanation: Find a safe gap to enter traffic smoothly. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep grade ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through at this speed.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show traffic laws you must obey. This sign shows the maximum speed limit. You may drive slower based on road conditions, but never faster.

questions.question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way.
Pedestrians must wait for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When facing a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green signal.
